records.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
records.overview: A simple suspension bridge crossing the Capilano River. It draws millions of visitors to walk above the canyon.
records.history_significance: Originally built in 1889 with hemp ropes. It is one of Vancouver's oldest and most famous tourist attractions, symbolizing the region's rugged nature.
records.highlights:
The swaying bridge 70 meters above the river.
 The Cliffwalk.
 The Treetops Adventure.

records.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
records.overview: A simple suspension bridge crossing the Capilano River in the District of North Vancouver, measuring 140 meters long and 70 meters above the river.
records.history_significance: Originally built in 1889 using hemp ropes and cedar planks, it was completely rebuilt in 1956 and has become one of British Columbia's most popular attractions.
records.highlights:
Walking across the gently swaying suspension bridge high above the river
 Exploring the Treetops Adventure suspended between old-growth Douglas firs
 Experiencing the thrilling Cliffwalk cantilevered out from the granite cliff

records.name: Cape of Good Hope
records.overview: A rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula in South Africa, known for its spectacular scenery.
records.highlights:

Spotting ostriches and baboons in the nature reserve.
Taking the funicular to the Cape Point lighthouse.

identical_except_name.name: Arch of Galerius
identical_except_name.overview: A monumental triumphal arch located at the junction of the Rotunda. It is one of the most famous Roman monuments in the city.
identical_except_name.history_significance: Built in the early 4th century AD to commemorate Emperor Galerius's victory over the Persians. The marble panels depict the battles.
identical_except_name.highlights:
The well-preserved marble panels and bas-reliefs.
 The Roman columns.
 Its position connecting the Via Regia.
